limitations: Measurements are specific to this shared macOS/Docker Linux host and synthetic x264 720p30 source; they are not embedded-hardware resource guarantees.
Three repetitions per condition provide ranges of paired observations, not a formal confidence interval or universal regression budget.
CPU ratios are fractions of one logical core; source, distribution and browser costs are reported separately.

Memory uses the measurement source reported per component. Docker cgroup usage can include recording tmpfs pages; process PSS/RSS fallback excludes the file storage, whose bytes are reported separately.
Negative paired differences are retained and indicate variation; they are not evidence that enabling a feature reduces its inherent cost.
The pixel marker changes source content slightly. Both profiles use explicit I420 caps and otherwise identical pipeline/configuration; production pipelines do not contain the marker.
Latency covers the marker before encoding to browser composition; physical exposure and display scanout are excluded.
Recordings use a bounded tmpfs: this compares memory-backed recording overhead, not sustained physical-disk or cloud-volume I/O latency.
This unshaped, one-reader comparison does not replace loss/capacity, full-storage or multiple-reader qualification.

method.source: Synthetic x264 H264 constrained-baseline, explicit I420, 1280x720 at 30 fps; adaptive encoder settles at 8000 kbit/s in every measured baseline.
method.topology: One source, one custom adapter/MediaMTX 1.21.1 instance, one Chromium viewer on one macOS-hosted Docker Linux VM. No artificial network impairment.
method.recording: fMP4, 1s parts, 5s target segments, 5m retention, 512 MiB bounded tmpfs; playback endpoint disabled.
method.probe: Qualification-only pre-encoding pixel timestamp and browser crop readback. Disabled in production.
method.resourceScope: Only batches wholly within the stable baseline phase. CPU is a fraction of one logical core. Cgroup memory includes tmpfs storage, not only process RSS.
